# Validation of the maximum-likelihood binormal fit

This report checks `smooth(method = "binormal")`, the maximum-likelihood fit
of the binormal model $\Phi^{-1}(TPF) = a + b \Phi^{-1}(FPF)$, against the
published results of ROCFIT, the maximum-likelihood program of Metz. It is
maintainer-only: knit it from the package root with the version of pROC to
check installed:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rmarkdown::render("tools/binormal_validation.Rmd")
# or on one core (Windows):
rmarkdown::render("tools/binormal_validation.Rmd", params = list(cores = 1))
```

It takes a few minutes on 4 cores.

Sources:

- **D&A**: Dorfman DD, Alf E (1969) Maximum-likelihood estimation of
  parameters of signal-detection theory and determination of confidence
  intervals — rating-method data. *J Math Psychol* 6:487–496.
- **D&B**: Dorfman DD, Berbaum KS (1995) Degeneracy and discrete receiver
  operating characteristic rating data. *Acad Radiol* 2:907–915.

```{r setup}
library(pROC)
library(parallel)
B <- params$B
cores <- params$cores
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
set.seed(20261106)
c(pROC = as.character(packageVersion("pROC")), R = R.version.string)
```

## Design

D&B (p. 909) sample five-category datasets from the population of Metz:
the binormal curve with $a = 1.5$ and $b = 0.8$, with the operating points
(FPF, TPF) = (0.00025, 0.10), (0.000328, 0.25), (0.03040, 0.50) and
(0.28114, 0.85). The FPF 0.000328 is not on the curve: a TPF of 0.25 needs
an FPF of 0.00328. The cut-points are taken from the TPFs, as in the report
of the proper fit. Each dataset is fitted with `method = "binormal"`; the
least-squares line on normal-deviate axes (the binormal smoothing of
pROC 1.19, and the start of the fit) is shown for comparison.

ROCFIT gives an exact fit with infinite parameters for degenerate datasets
and "does not compute diagnostic accuracy in such situations" (D&B p. 907);
D&B report its means on the non-degenerate datasets only. pROC refuses the
same data with an error (fewer than two points inside the square, or
points all on one horizontal or vertical line), so its means are taken over
the datasets it fits.

```{r design}
a <- 1.5
b <- 0.8
cuts <- sort((a - qnorm(c(0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.85))) / b)
true <- c(a = a, b = b, auc = pnorm(a / sqrt(1 + b^2)))
fpf.at <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
pa.bounds <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
# partial areas under TPF = pnorm(a + b * qnorm(FPF)) between the FPF bounds
partial.areas <- function(a, b) {
  vapply(1:4, function(i) {
    integrate(function(x) pnorm(a + b * qnorm(x)), pa.bounds[i], pa.bounds[i + 1])$value
  }, numeric(1))
}
one <- function(n.controls, n.cases) {
  r <- roc(
    controls = findInterval(rnorm(n.controls), cuts), cases = findInterval(rnorm(n.cases, a / b, 1 / b), cuts),
    direction = "<", quiet = TRUE
  )
  s <- tryCatch(smooth(r, method = "binormal"), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(s)) {
    return(rep(NA_real_, 12))
  }
  ml <- s$binormal
  df <- data.frame(sp = qnorm(r$specificities), se = qnorm(r$sensitivities))
  df <- df[is.finite(df$sp) & is.finite(df$se), ]
  ls <- pROC:::binormal_ls(df)
  c(
    a = ml$a, b = ml$b, auc = as.numeric(auc(s)),
    tpf = pnorm(ml$a + ml$b * qnorm(fpf.at)), pa = partial.areas(ml$a, ml$b),
    ls.a = ls[["a"]], ls.b = ls[["b"]]
  )
}
summarize <- function(x, true, published, published.rmse) {
  fitted <- !is.na(x[, 1])
  data.frame(
    true = true, mean = colMeans(x[fitted, , drop = FALSE]), published = published,
    rmse = sqrt(colMeans(sweep(x[fitted, , drop = FALSE], 2, true)^2)), published.rmse = published.rmse
  )
}
```

## Small datasets (D&B Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5)

1000 datasets of 30 negative and 40 positive cases in D&B; `r B` here.

```{r small, cache = TRUE}
small <- do.call(rbind, mclapply(seq_len(B), function(i) one(30, 40), mc.cores = cores))
refused <- is.na(small[, 1])
c(refused = mean(refused), rocfit.degenerate = 419 / 1000)
```

pROC refuses `r round(100 * mean(refused), 1)`% of the datasets; ROCFIT
classified 419 of 1000 as degenerate (D&B Table 1, p. 911).

The parameters and the area (D&B Table 3, p. 911, "Metz nondegenerate
samples (n = 581)"), the TPF at fixed FPFs (Table 4, p. 912) and the partial
areas (Table 5, p. 912), with ROCFIT's means and RMSEs on its 581
non-degenerate datasets:

```{r small-table}
knitr::kable(summarize(small[, 1:10],
  true = c(true, pnorm(a + b * qnorm(fpf.at)), partial.areas(a, b)),
  published = c(1.631, 0.948, 0.869, 0.528, 0.656, 0.785, 0.163, 0.221, 0.238, 0.246),
  published.rmse = c(0.5474, 0.3505, 0.0500, 0.1171, 0.1020, 0.0868, 0.0226, 0.0170, 0.0111, 0.0053)
), digits = 4)
```

The least-squares line on the same datasets:

```{r small-ls}
knitr::kable(summarize(small[, 11:12], true = true[1:2], published = c(NA, NA), published.rmse = c(NA, NA))[, c("true", "mean", "rmse")], digits = 4)
```

## Large datasets (D&B Table 2)

2000 negative and 2000 positive cases (D&B Table 2, p. 911: 1000 datasets).

```{r large, cache = TRUE}
large <- do.call(rbind, mclapply(seq_len(B), function(i) one(2000, 2000), mc.cores = cores))
sum(is.na(large[, 1]))
knitr::kable(summarize(large[, 1:3],
  true = true, published = c(1.499, 0.799, 0.879), published.rmse = c(0.0541, 0.0398, 0.0059)
), digits = 4)
```

## Discussion

```{r z, echo = FALSE}
published.small <- c(1.631, 0.948, 0.869, 0.528, 0.656, 0.785, 0.163, 0.221, 0.238, 0.246)
fitted <- small[!refused, 1:10]
# SE of the difference of the means: the simulation error of both (ROCFIT's
# from its 581 datasets), and the rounding of the published means to 3
# decimals as a uniform error of +-0.0005
z.small <- (colMeans(fitted) - published.small) /
  sqrt(apply(fitted, 2, var) * (1 / nrow(fitted) + 1 / 581) + 0.0005^2 / 3)
rmse <- function(x, true) sqrt(colMeans(sweep(x, 2, true)^2))
rmse.ratio <- rmse(fitted[, 1:3], true) / c(0.5474, 0.3505, 0.0500)
ls <- small[!refused, 11:12]
```

**Degenerate data.** pROC refuses about as many datasets as ROCFIT
classifies as degenerate (`r round(100 * mean(refused), 1)`% against 41.9%,
`r sprintf("%.1f", abs(mean(refused) - 0.419) / sqrt(0.419 * 0.581 * (1 / 1000 + 1 / B)))`
SE apart). ROCFIT's classes of degeneracy are only given in its code (D&B
p. 907), and D&B may have generated the counts at the published operating
points rather than at the cut-points of the curve.

**Small datasets.** On the datasets pROC fits, the means of $a$, $b$, the
area, the TPFs and the partial areas agree with ROCFIT's on its
non-degenerate datasets within `r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(z.small)))` SE
(counting the simulation error of both, and the rounding of the published
means). With so few cases both
overestimate $a$ and $b$ and slightly underestimate the area. The RMSEs of
$a$, $b$ and the area are `r round(100 * (1 - max(rmse.ratio)))`% to
`r round(100 * (1 - min(rmse.ratio)))`% lower than ROCFIT's.

**Large datasets.** The means and RMSEs agree with ROCFIT's.

**Least squares.** The least-squares line, the binormal smoothing of
pROC 1.19 and the start of the fit, overestimates $a$ and $b$ more (means
`r sprintf("%.3f", colMeans(ls)[1])` and `r sprintf("%.3f", colMeans(ls)[2])`),
with larger RMSEs (`r sprintf("%.3f", rmse(ls, true[1:2])[1])` and
`r sprintf("%.3f", rmse(ls, true[1:2])[2])`). It is not a maximum-likelihood
estimate: D&A (p. 491) note that an "eyeball" fit on normal-deviate axes
"would not coincide with the fit based upon the MLE".
